lesson.subject: general-knowledge
lesson.title: Brave and Clever People
lesson.summary: Meet people from different times who changed the world with careful thinking and kindness.
learning_objectives: Say who a significant person is
Describe how one person changed things
Sort people by what they did

standards.text: Learn about the lives of significant individuals in the past who have contributed to national and international achievements

success_criteria: I can say what significant means
I can say what Al-Razi, Ada and Marie did
I can make a fact card about a hero
lesson.real_life: Al-Razi from Persia and the Baghdad hospital, Abdul Sattar Edhi in Karachi, and Florence Nightingale and Mary Seacole in Britain. Adult support is suggested because the lesson talks about illness.

warm_up.prompt: Who helps us when we are ill?
warm_up.explanation: A doctor helps when we are ill.

warm_up.prompt: Books can keep ideas for a long time.

blocks.markdown: Today's big question: how did one person change the world?
blocks.say: Today we meet brave and clever people. They helped others with careful thinking.

blocks.alt: A very old, worn leather book with a decorated spine and gold-edged pages on a dark cloth
blocks.caption: An old leather book. Doctors long ago wrote their discoveries in books like this.
blocks.credit: Photo by Danika Perkinson on Unsplash
blocks.say: This old book is very worn. Long ago, doctors wrote down what they learned.

blocks.markdown: A **significant** person changed the world in an important way.
blocks.say: Al-Razi was a famous doctor from Persia, over a thousand years ago.
He watched patients very closely. He wrote down what he saw.

scenes.caption: Careful.
scenes.say: Al-Razi watched each patient carefully. He wrote down the signs.

scenes.caption: Compare.
scenes.say: He compared different illnesses. He learned which was which.

scenes.caption: Medicine.
scenes.say: Careful looking helps doctors choose the right medicine.

question.explanation: To observe is to watch carefully.

blocks.alt: A bright, clean hospital corridor with white walls, benches and many closed doors
blocks.caption: A clean, bright hospital corridor. Al-Razi chose a clean place for sick people.
blocks.credit: Photo by Tasha Kostyuk on Unsplash
blocks.say: Al-Razi worked in a hospital in Baghdad. He cared for everyone.

blocks.markdown: A good doctor helps everyone who needs care.
blocks.say: He helped rich people and poor people. Kindness for all was important.

scenes.caption: Hospital.
scenes.say: A hospital is a place where doctors and nurses care for sick people.

scenes.caption: Everyone.
scenes.say: Al-Razi treated people who could pay, and people who could not.

scenes.caption: Edhi.
scenes.say: In Karachi, Abdul Sattar Edhi also helped the poor.

blocks.title: Zainab meets Al-Razi
blocks.transcript: Zainab opens an old book from Baghdad. Inside she meets Al-Razi, a famous doctor. He watches his patients closely. He tests medicines carefully, so they help. He chooses a clean place for the hospital. He cares for rich people and poor people. Zainab also learns about Ada and Marie. She makes a card about a hero in her own life.
blocks.caption: Zainab opens an old book from Baghdad and meets Al-Razi, who tested medicines and chose a clean place for a hospital.

points: He cared for rich and poor
blocks.say: Let us remember. Al-Razi observed carefully and cared for all.

terms.meaning: Important, because it changed something.
A person who helps sick people get better.
To watch carefully.
Something a doctor gives to help us get well.
A place where sick people are cared for.
A great city in Iraq with a famous old hospital.

options.text: A person who helps sick people
A place where sick people are cared for

mini_quiz.prompt: Why did Al-Razi write things down?

blocks.markdown: Ada Lovelace imagined what machines could do.
blocks.say: Ada Lovelace lived in Britain about two hundred years ago. She loved numbers.

blocks.markdown: A **program** is a set of instructions for a machine.
blocks.say: She wrote the first idea for a computer program. It was for a machine.

scenes.caption: Maths.
scenes.say: Ada loved maths and wrote careful notes.

scenes.caption: Instructions.
scenes.say: She imagined a machine that could follow instructions.

scenes.caption: A program.
scenes.say: Today we call these instructions a program.

blocks.alt: A bright white laboratory bench with a microscope, test tube racks and scientific equipment
blocks.caption: A laboratory with a microscope. Marie Curie worked in a lab to learn about radioactivity.
blocks.credit: Photo by Trnava University on Unsplash
blocks.say: Marie Curie studied a new kind of energy. She worked in a laboratory.

blocks.markdown: A **scientist** finds out how the world works.
blocks.say: She won the Nobel Prize, a very special prize. She won it twice.

scenes.caption: Hard work.
scenes.say: Marie worked hard, even when it was difficult.

scenes.caption: Sharing.
scenes.say: She shared her ideas so others could learn.

scenes.caption: Helping.
scenes.say: Her work helped doctors see inside the body.

blocks.title: Health or ideas?
blocks.goal: Move each person. A doctor goes in Health. A scientist goes in Ideas.
blocks.say: Sort the people. Did each one help with Health or Science ideas?

question.prompt: Marie Curie worked in a laboratory.
question.explanation: Marie Curie was a scientist in a lab.

points: Both worked hard and shared ideas
blocks.say: Let us remember. Ada imagined computers. Marie Curie lit up science.

terms.meaning: A set of instructions for a machine.
A person who finds out how the world works.

blocks.say: Let us play Who am I? Listen to the clues and guess the person.

scenes.caption: Clue 1.
scenes.say: Clue one: I was a doctor in Baghdad. I watched patients carefully.

scenes.caption: Clue 2.
scenes.say: Clue two: I helped the rich and the poor. Who am I?

scenes.caption: Answer.
scenes.say: I am Al-Razi, the doctor who cared for everyone.

blocks.markdown: A hero can be a teacher, a neighbour or a family member.
blocks.say: A hero is someone who helps others. They do not have to be famous.
